text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.6% today, continuing a three-day rally that's erased most of last week's losses. The move follows Trump administration statements over the past two days suggesting the Iran conflict is winding down—Trump said Monday the war would end "fairly soon" and that "Iran militarily is effectively over." Oil prices have already reacted to that rhetoric: Brent crude briefly dipped below $90 a barrel for the first time since August, though US crude is still holding near $90. For an oil company, lower geopolitical risk and stabilizing (if not surging) crude prices create a more predictable environment, which the market is rewarding.

The stock's recovery also comes after CNBC highlighted ConocoPhillips among "the biggest calls of the day" on November 11th, suggesting fresh analyst or investor attention. The broader energy sector has been volatile on Iran headlines, but the narrative has shifted from escalation risk toward de-escalation, which removes a major source of uncertainty that had weighed on the stock through early November.
